clips.send: In this front view of the white marble tomb, the dome and main entrance share a centerline. Matching towers and openings keep your gaze balanced on both sides.
clips.text: In this front view of the white marble tomb, the dome and main entrance share a centerline. Matching towers and openings keep your gaze balanced on both sides.

clips.send: This plaster cast is in Gallery 3 of the Fitzwilliam Museum in Cambridge, England. The original relief came from the fifth-century BCE Parthenon. Rotate the cast sideways and see how far the figures stand out.

clips.send: A round arch spans an opening. In Rome’s Pantheon, a dome curves over a circular room. Daylight enters through the oculus at its crown.
clips.text: A round arch spans an opening. In Rome’s Pantheon, a dome curves over a circular room. Daylight enters through the oculus at its crown.

clips.send: The roof shells repeat related curves. Their shapes come from different pieces of the same sphere.
clips.text: The roof shells repeat related curves. Their shapes come from different pieces of the same sphere.

clips.send: Pick a piece and tap a slot to place it. Put a door in the center and make the three slots on either side mirror each other. You may leave spaces blank. Use at least one pair of openings.
clips.text: Pick a piece and tap a slot to place it. Put a door in the center and make the three slots on either side mirror each other. You may leave spaces blank. Use at least one pair of openings.

clips.send: The curves of a pointed arch meet at a peak. Tall stained-glass windows color daylight and draw your eyes up. In “The Blue Virgin,” the light-blue central panels date to the 12th century. The surrounding glass is from the 13th century.

clips.send: The arm extends sideways from its seat. Look for the smaller blocks that rest on its ends.
clips.text: The arm extends sideways from its seat. Look for the smaller blocks that rest on its ends.

clips.send: A round opening makes a picture out of what lies beyond it. This is framing, or kuàngjǐng.
clips.text: A round opening makes a picture out of what lies beyond it. This is framing, or kuàngjǐng.

clips.send: The North Temple Pagoda rises beyond the garden. From this viewpoint it becomes part of the scene, an example of borrowed scenery.
clips.text: The North Temple Pagoda rises beyond the garden. From this viewpoint it becomes part of the scene, an example of borrowed scenery.

clips.send: Repeated openings give a wall a visual beat. Your eyes can sense an interval just as your ears sense a pause.
clips.text: Repeated openings give a wall a visual beat. Your eyes can sense an interval just as your ears sense a pause.

clips.send: Proportion is a relationship between sizes. Keep the opening the same width and change its height.
clips.text: Proportion is a relationship between sizes. Keep the opening the same width and change its height.

clips.send: A row of gates draws your eye into the distance. A window turns a garden into a picture. When you face a building, what do you notice first? What makes you stop?
clips.text: A row of gates draws your eye into the distance. A window turns a garden into a picture. When you face a building, what do you notice first? What makes you stop?

clips.send: Major gates and halls line up on a north–south axis. From the front of the Hall of Supreme Harmony, the stairs and roof ridge draw your eye toward the center. The plan simplifies the layout.
clips.text: Major gates and halls line up on a north–south axis. From the front of the Hall of Supreme Harmony, the stairs and roof ridge draw your eye toward the center. The plan simplifies the layout.

clips.send: A vertical line can act like a mirror. Try moving just one window and see how the balance changes.
clips.text: A vertical line can act like a mirror. Try moving just one window and see how the balance changes.

clips.send: A patch of light can lead your eye across a dark room. Shift the beam and see which part becomes the focus.
clips.text: A patch of light can lead your eye across a dark room. Shift the beam and see which part becomes the focus.

clips.send: Crossing steel members create a web of diagonals. Follow one line and let a second take over.
clips.text: Crossing steel members create a web of diagonals. Follow one line and let a second take over.

clips.send: Eight columns line each short end, and seventeen line each long side, counting the corner columns on both sides. The platform at the columns is about 69.5 m long and 30.9 m wide. The long side is about 2.25 times the short side.

clips.send: The upper timber rests across the smaller blocks in the model. Slide the layers together to see the contacts.
clips.text: The upper timber rests across the smaller blocks in the model. Slide the layers together to see the contacts.

clips.send: Keep the shape and change the surface. Stone joints, wood grain and bright reflections lead the eye in different ways.
clips.text: Keep the shape and change the surface. Stone joints, wood grain and bright reflections lead the eye in different ways.

clips.send: Look under the eaves for layers of blocks and arms. In this simplified dougong model, they step out from the top of a wooden column.
clips.text: Look under the eaves for layers of blocks and arms. In this simplified dougong model, they step out from the top of a wooden column.

clips.send: Follow the roof edge to the corner, where the line lifts. Trace it with your finger and feel it change from a gentle slope to an upward sweep.
clips.text: Follow the roof edge to the corner, where the line lifts. Trace it with your finger and feel it change from a gentle slope to an upward sweep.

clips.send: Long concrete terraces reach out over a waterfall. Their horizontal edges echo the layers of rock.
clips.text: Long concrete terraces reach out over a waterfall. Their horizontal edges echo the layers of rock.

clips.send: Some sound reflects from walls, floors and ceilings. When many reflections overlap, sound can linger after its source stops. This is called reverberation.
clips.text: Some sound reflects from walls, floors and ceilings. When many reflections overlap, sound can linger after its source stops. This is called reverberation.

clips.send: At a new viewpoint, a different opening catches your eye. This unfolding of views as you move is yíbù huànjǐng.
clips.text: At a new viewpoint, a different opening catches your eye. This unfolding of views as you move is yíbù huànjǐng.

clips.send: A block sits above the column in this model. Its seat receives the arm and helps keep it in place.
clips.text: A block sits above the column in this model. Its seat receives the arm and helps keep it in place.

clips.send: 一排门把你的目光引向远处，一扇窗把园林变成一幅画。面对一座建筑，你第一眼看见什么？是什么让你停下来？

clips.send: 顺着屋檐边缘看向角部，轮廓向上挑起。手指沿着这条线比划一下，感受它从平缓到上扬的变化。

clips.send: 拱从斗口向两侧伸出。找一找拱的两端各托着什么。
clips.text: 拱从斗口向两侧伸出。找一找拱的两端各托着什么。

clips.send: 模型中的斗位于柱头上。斗口托住拱，使它能坐稳。
clips.text: 模型中的斗位于柱头上。斗口托住拱，使它能坐稳。

clips.send: 长长的混凝土露台伸到瀑布上方，水平边缘与层层岩石相呼应。

clips.send: 这是剑桥菲茨威廉博物馆第 3 展厅展出的石膏翻模。原浮雕来自公元前 5 世纪的帕特农神庙。把模型转到侧面，看看人物浮雕凸起了多少。

clips.send: 北寺塔立在园外。从这个视点看，它却成了眼前景色的一部分，这就是借景。

clips.send: 圆拱跨过开口。罗马万神殿的穹顶覆盖圆形大厅，自然光从顶端的圆形天窗照进来。

clips.send: 月洞门把门后的景物收进一幅画里。这种手法叫框景。

clips.send: 故宫的主要殿门和大殿沿南北中轴排列。观察太和殿正面，台阶和屋脊把目光引向中央。示意图只画出布局的主要关系。

clips.send: 屋顶壳体的曲线彼此呼应，形状取自同一个球面的不同部分。

clips.send: 一条竖线可以像镜面一样。只移动一扇窗，看看左右的平衡感怎么变。
clips.text: 一条竖线可以像镜面一样。只移动一扇窗，看看左右的平衡感怎么变。

clips.send: 比例是各部分大小之间的关系。保持开口的宽度不变，只改变高度。
clips.text: 比例是各部分大小之间的关系。保持开口的宽度不变，只改变高度。

clips.send: 先选构件，再点一个格子放下它。中间放门，左右各排三个构件，做成镜面对称。可以有留白，但至少要有一对开口。
clips.text: 先选构件，再点一个格子放下它。中间放门，左右各排三个构件，做成镜面对称。可以有留白，但至少要有一对开口。

clips.send: 当声音遇到墙面、地面和天花板，会有一部分反射回来。许多反射声叠在一起，原声停止后还会短暂延续，这叫混响。

clips.send: 保持形状不变，只换表面。石缝、木纹和反光引导视线的方式各不相同。

clips.send: 抬头看檐下层层叠置的斗和拱。这个简化模型展示木构件怎样从柱头向外一层层挑出。

clips.text: 重复的开口给墙面带来视觉节奏。眼睛能察觉间隔，就像耳朵能听出停顿一样。
